narrative.overview: BuildPath is a maker's drafting table at golden hour — warm and precise. The surfaces are aged oak and dark walnut, never cold; the line currently being drawn carries warm amber light, like a brass instrument catching lamp glow. Structure still does the talking — hairline rules, tabular numerals, consistent radii — but the temperature is workshop, not server room. Think Aesop packaging, not GitHub dashboard.
keyCharacteristics: Warm dark surfaces (aged oak → walnut → raised brown), every gray brown-shifted
One illuminated element per screen; the light is amber, like a task lamp
Terracotta for the single forward action; amber for state, progress, and focus
Editorial typography: Playfair Display serif headings over an Inter body
Tight 6px radii, hairline dividers, paper-like cards

rules.name: The One Lit Line Rule
rules.body: Amber glow may appear only on the timeline and the current phase's card, node, and connector. Two glowing elements on one screen means one is wrong.

rules.name: The Terracotta Means Go Rule
rules.body: Terracotta appears on exactly one affordance per screen: the action that moves the project forward.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: No blue-shifted gray survives review. If a neutral's hue isn't brown, it's a bug.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every changing number keeps font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums in the mono stack so reflow never wobbles.

dos: Do spend the amber glow budget on the current phase only.
Do keep terracotta to one forward action per screen, always with dark #1a1714 text.
Do brown-shift every neutral — canvas, borders, shadows, text all carry the warm hue.
Do keep cards paper-like: warm fills and hairlines, no glass, no blur.
Do keep every animation's prefers-reduced-motion alternative.
donts: Don't use cold blues, cyans, or blue-grays anywhere — including the old #49c4d8/#050a0d family and the original #3b82f6/#f97316 defaults.
Don't let any hue except amber and terracotta reach full brightness.
Don't ship the generic SaaS dashboard, neon overload, or sterile gray.
Don't use Ink Muted (#6b5f52) for running text — hints only.
Don't put white text on amber or terracotta fills — both carry dark text.
